hypothesis: Measure a fresh postbreach mixed-language held-out pool before any new adapter design, keeping thinking enabled and inspecting only aggregate eval output.
verdict: Baseline is valid but difficult: composite 0.2996 is just below the router's strictness threshold, while outcome is 0.5000 and format_compliance 0.5625. Because convention_consistency and read_before_edit are saturated, next step is a train-rollout rubric audit before choosing SFT/GRPO; eval task contents and per-example eval rollouts were not inspected.
notes: Postbreach split generated 32 train / 16 eval / 12 hard_eval tasks across js_camel_warn_jsdoc, py_camel_loose, py_strict_typed_snake, and rust_snake_result. Rubric sanity separation was +0.5833. No eval task contents or per-example eval transcripts were inspected.

hypothesis: Verifier-backed ideal train traces across all postbreach profiles should bootstrap the complete read/edit/verify/final rhythm and lift both outcome and final format from the fresh baseline.
notes: No eval task contents or per-example eval transcripts were inspected. A train-rollout audit before training showed true outcome and missing-final-response failures, so the low baseline was not just rubric over-strictness. The SFT arm lifted outcome slightly but damaged format, convention, read-before-edit, and efficiency.
verdict: Rejected: blind 3-seed eval regressed composite from 0.2996 to 0.1954. Outcome rose only from 0.5000 to 0.5417, while format_compliance fell from 0.5625 to 0.4583, convention_consistency fell from 0.9736 to 0.9306, read_before_edit fell from 1.0000 to 0.9583, wall-clock more than doubled, and tool/thinking usage increased. This falsifies single-distribution ideal trace SFT as the first postbreach stage.
